question: The Poligar Rebellion took place in which part of India? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (27/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Tamil Nadu
Maharashtra
Bengal
Punjab
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tamil Nadu

Explanation:
The Poligar Rebellion was a peasant uprising against the British East India Company that took place in the southern districts of Tamil Nadu. It lasted from 1799 to 1805 and was led by Poligars (feudal chiefs). The main causes were excessive taxes and company control over agricultural lands. Key leaders included Veeramundi and Puli Thevar. The rebellion was eventually suppressed by the Company's army, but it laid the groundwork for the Indian independence movement.

question: Which among the following battles in 1757 marked the beginning of British political control in India? (RRB Technician Grade III (10/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Battle of Buxar
Battle of Colachel
Battle of Seringapatam
Battle of Plassey
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Battle of Plassey

Explanation:
The Battle of Plassey fought in 1757 marked the beginning of British political control in India. In this battle, the British East India Company led by Robert Clive defeated the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah. The company used conspirators like Mir Jafar to its advantage. After this victory, the British East India Company gained political authority in Bengal and transformed from a trading company into a ruling power. This battle laid the foundation of colonial rule in India.

question: At which session of the Indian National Congress did the party formally split into the Moderates and the Extremists? (RRB Technician Grade III (06/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Delhi session 1912
Calcutta session 1906
Bombay session 1910
Surat session 1907
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Surat session 1907

Explanation:
The Indian National Congress session at Surat in 1907 witnessed the formal split of the party into the Moderates and the Extremists. The Moderates were led by Gopal Krishna Gokhale, while the Extremists were led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak. The main reasons for the split were differences over the approach to national education, the Swadeshi movement, and the proposal by Tilak for the party presidency. This split marked a significant turning point in the history of the Congress, leading to separate strategies by both factions. The session is historically important as it divided the national movement into two distinct ideological streams.

question: Who among the following were the pivotal leaders of the Santhal Rebellion of 1855–1856? (RRB Technician Grade III (09/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Tilka Manjhi and Sido Kanhu
Birsa Munda and Raghunath Murmu
Lalu Prasad and Sidhu Kanhu
Sidhu Murmu and Kanhu Murmu
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sidhu Murmu and Kanhu Murmu

Explanation:
The Santhal Rebellion of 1855-1856 was a major tribal uprising against British rule by the Santhal community. The leaders of this rebellion were Sidhu Murmu and Kanhu Murmu, two of the four Murmu brothers. They organized the revolt in the Bhagalpur region (present-day Jharkhand) against oppressive British taxation and the zamindari system. Around 10,000 Santhals participated in the rebellion. Both brothers fought valiantly but were eventually killed in 1856. This uprising remains a significant example of tribal resistance against colonial exploitation.

question: Which among the following slogans was popularised by Bal Gangadhar Tilak? (RRB Paramedical (13/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it
Give me blood and I will give you freedom
Freedom is our goal and we shall achieve it
Liberty is our dream and we must attain it
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it

Explanation:
Bal Gangadhar Tilak popularised the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'. This slogan became a rallying cry in the Indian freedom struggle. Tilak was a staunch nationalist and a strong advocate of Swaraj (self-rule). He inspired Indians to demand self-governance as their birthright. Through his writings in 'Kesari' and public speeches, he spread this message widely. Tilak was a leader of the extremist faction in the Indian National Congress. His slogan ignited the spirit of patriotism among millions. The concept of Swaraj was central to his political philosophy. Tilak believed that Indians had an inherent right to rule themselves and must fight to achieve it.

question: In which year was the East India Company founded to engage in trade with India and East and Southeast Asia? (RRB Paramedical (12/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: 1610
1605
1600
1615
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1600

Explanation:
The East India Company was founded on 31 December 1600 under a Royal Charter granted by Queen Elizabeth I of England. Its primary objective was to engage in trade with India and East and Southeast Asia, particularly in spices, silk, cotton, and other valuable commodities. The company was originally known as the 'Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies'. Over time, it became the foundation of British colonial rule in India, exerting economic and political influence for over 250 years until the British Crown took direct control in 1858.

question: Which of the following cities became the capital of British India in the late 18th century? (RRB Paramedical (12/03/2026) Shift 2)

Bombay
Kolkata
Madras
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kolkata

question: In which year did the Vellore Mutiny take place? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (24/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: 1817 CE
1857 CE
1799 CE
1806 CE
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1806 CE

Explanation:
The Vellore Mutiny took place on 10 July 1806 CE. It was the first major mutiny by Indian sepoys against the British East India Company. The immediate cause was the new dress code and headgear regulations for sepoys, which banned turbans and required leather caps believed to be made from animal fat. The revolt occurred at Vellore Fort and lasted about 24 hours. It was crushed by artillery and cavalry under Colonel Gillespie, resulting in over 100 British and more than 350 Indian deaths. The mutiny highlighted early resentment against British cultural and religious insensitivity.

question: Under which policy were Indian rulers required to dissolve their own armed forces and accept the British East India Company in their territories, and bear the cost of maintaining those forces? (RRB Paramedical (12/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Policy of Mercantilism
Policy of Neutrality
Policy of Paramountcy
Subsidiary Alliance
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Subsidiary Alliance

Explanation:
The Subsidiary Alliance was a policy introduced by Lord Wellesley (1798-1805). Under this, Indian rulers were required to disband their own armies and accept British troops within their territories. The ruler had to bear the cost of maintaining these troops, often leading to financial drain. Additionally, the ruler lost control over foreign policy, as they had to consult the British East India Company on all external matters. This policy was instrumental in expanding British influence in India. States like Hyderabad, Awadh, Pune, and Mysore were forced to accept this alliance, which effectively ended their sovereignty.

question: Which of the following incidents led to the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement? (RRB Paramedical (11/03/2026) Shift 2)

Explanation:
The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in 1920 under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. On February 5, 1922, in the village of Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district, Uttar Pradesh, protesters set fire to a police station, killing 22 policemen. This violent incident deeply disturbed Gandhi, and he called off the Non-Cooperation Movement on February 12, 1922. He believed the nation was not yet ready for non-violent struggle. The Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919) was a cause of the movement, the Dandi March (1930) was part of the Salt Satyagraha, and the Simon Commission (1928) led to the demand for Purna Swaraj.

question: Which port did the Portuguese capture in 1510, making it their colony’s capital in India? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (19/03/2026) Shift 2)

solution:

Explanation:

After capturing Goa, Albuquerque fortified it and made it the headquarters of the Portuguese empire in India. This event was a significant milestone in the colonial expansion of European powers in India.

question: Which of the following cities did Vasco da Gama first reach in India after discovering the all-sea route from Europe? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (25/03/2026) Shift 1)

Surat

Explanation:
Vasco da Gama discovered the all-sea route from Europe to India in 1498 by rounding the Cape of Good Hope in Africa. He departed from Portugal and crossed the Indian Ocean, landing at the port of Calicut (now Kozhikode, Kerala) on the western coast of India. At that time, Calicut was a major trading center, particularly for spices like black pepper. The Zamorin (ruler) of Calicut initially welcomed da Gama, although later conflicts arose over trade. While Goa, Diu, and Surat later became associated with Portuguese activities, da Gama's first landing point in India was Calicut. This discovery broke the monopoly of Arab and Venetian traders and opened the way for European colonial expansion in Asia.

question: Which of the following principle was most emphasized by Bal Gangadhar Tilak during the Extremist Phase? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Support for communal representation
Swaraj as the birthright of every Indian
Exclusive focus on economic reforms
Complete armed revolution against the British
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Swaraj as the birthright of every Indian

Explanation:
During the Extremist Phase (1905-1908), Bal Gangadhar Tilak emphasized that Swaraj (self-rule) was the birthright of every Indian. He popularized the slogan, 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it.' Tilak viewed Swaraj not just as political independence but as a symbol of self-reliance and national pride. He mobilized mass support through the Home Rule League (1916) and used traditional festivals like Ganesh Chaturthi to spread nationalist ideas. Unlike moderates, he rejected reliance on British benevolence and advocated for direct action and resistance. However, he did not support complete armed revolution but favored constitutional agitation and mass movements. His emphasis on Swaraj as a birthright became the core ideology of the Indian freedom struggle.

question_hi: चरमपंथी चरण के दौरान बाल गंगाधर तिलक ने निम्नलिखित में से किस सिद्धांत पर सर्वाधिक जोर दिया था? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 1)
options_hi: सांप्रदायिक प्रतिनिधित्व के लिए सपोर्ट
स्वराज प्रत्येक भारतीय का जन्मसिद्ध अधिकार
आर्थिक सुधारों पर विशेष ध्यान
ब्रिटिश के विरुद्ध पूर्ण सशस्त्र क्रांति
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है स्वराज प्रत्येक भारतीय का जन्मसिद्ध अधिकार

Explanation:
चरमपंथी चरण (1905-1908) के दौरान बाल गंगाधर तिलक ने स्वराज को भारतीयों का जन्मसिद्ध अधिकार बताया। उन्होंने कहा, 'स्वराज मेरा जन्मसिद्ध अधिकार है और मैं इसे लेकर रहूंगा।' तिलक ने स्वराज को केवल राजनीतिक स्वतंत्रता नहीं, बल्कि आत्मनिर्भरता और राष्ट्रीय गौरव का प्रतीक माना। उन्होंने होम रूल लीग (1916) की स्थापना कर स्वराज के लिए जन जागरण किया। आर्थिक सुधार या सांप्रदायिक प्रतिनिधित्व पर जोर देने के बजाय उन्होंने राजनीतिक स्वतंत्रता को प्राथमिकता दी। वे ब्रिटिश शासन के खिलाफ जन आंदोलन और प्रतिरोध के पक्षधर थे, लेकिन पूर्ण सशस्त्र क्रांति के समर्थक नहीं थे।
